title: Lifting Equipment & Operations
whatItIs: Lifting equipment includes cranes, hoists, forklifts, MEWPs and accessories such as chains, slings and eyebolts. LOLER 1998 covers how lifts are run and how kit is examined.

keyFacts.text: Every lift MUST be planned by a competent person, properly supervised and carried out safely.
Lifting machinery and accessories MUST be clearly marked with their safe working load.
If a thorough examination finds a dangerous defect, the kit MUST NOT be used until the defect is put right.

keyFacts: Never stand under a load. Plan load routes so loads are not lifted over people.
The crane supervisor should not be the crane operator, and can stop the lift if it is unsafe.
Never ride on a goods-only hoist.

visual.caption: Thorough examination by a competent person (LOLER reg 9)

notes: Or follow an examination scheme drawn up by a competent person.

a.label: Crane hire
points: You plan and supervise the lift

b.label: Contract lift
points: Hire company is responsible for safety

onTheTest.question: Unless an examination scheme says otherwise, how often must slings and chains be thoroughly examined?
onTheTest.why: LOLER reg 9(3): accessories and kit for lifting people at least every 6 months; other lifting equipment every 12 months.

onTheTest.question: A crane is lifting a bundle of steel across the site. Where should you be?
options: Underneath it, ready to steady it
Out of its path, never under it
Riding on the load to guide it
onTheTest.why: HSG150 paras 311, 332: do not stand under loads; plan load routes so loads are not lifted over people.

traps: No lift is too small to plan.
Wider sling angles mean more load in each leg, not less.
Never use makeshift hooks such as bent reinforcing bar.
Doubt the load's weight or the kit? Don't lift.
